name: Axillary sweat gland suction
lead: Axillary sweat gland suction, also called suction-curettage or liposuction-type removal, is a minor surgical approach to underarm sweating in which sweat glands in the armpit are physically removed or disrupted through small incisions [1].

Wikipedia's hyperhidrosis article lists axillary sweat gland removal or destruction by suction, curettage, liposuction-type removal or laser ablation among surgical options [1]. Related procedures are also used for underarm odor (osmidrosis) [3].
The available record contains two small registered trials and no published results summaries, so evidence for this entry in this wiki is limited to what those registrations describe.

paras: Surgical approaches remove or destroy the glands rather than blocking their nerve signal. Reference sources group suction, curettage and laser ablation together as axillary gland procedures [1].

A registered trial (NCT01274611, 20 participants, started 2010) studied botulinum toxin and suction-curettage for axillary hyperhidrosis [2]. Another registration (NCT01539460, 30 participants, started 2012, status unknown) examined combined liposuction with subcutaneous pruning for axillary osmidrosis [3]. Results are not described in the available record.
Specific adverse-event data for this procedure are not available in the reviewed material.

card.note: Surgical procedure; outcome data in available sources are sparse.

quick.overview:
Axillary sweat gland suction is a minor surgery in which armpit sweat glands are removed or disrupted using suction or curettage. It is used for heavy underarm sweating and sometimes for underarm odor.

Only small registered trials appear in the available record, without published results.
quick.mechanism: Physically removing or destroying the glands means they can no longer produce sweat.
quick.risks: Surgical risks apply in general; specific complication data were not available in the reviewed sources.
